source.title: RAJ-PGA: Reasoning-Activated Jailbreak and Principle-Guided Alignment Framework for Large Reasoning Models
source.authors: Jianhao Chen; Mayi Xu; Haoyang Chen; Xiaohu Li; Xiangyu Zhang; Jianjie Huang; Zheng Wang; Xiaochun Cao; Tieyun Qian

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports outcomes for a reasoning-activated prompt-concretization jailbreak on LRMs, a distinct attack mechanism and setting from the claim’s specified interventions and first-token mechanism.
record.gate_note: The paper measures concretization-based jailbreak outcomes, including changes in unsafe-response rates. It does not measure aligned-versus-base per-token KL, compliant-token prefilling, suffixes, decoding changes, small-data harmful or benign fine-tuning as specified by the claim, or whether safety is concentrated in a small parameter set. Fine-tuning on the deliberately unsafe RAJ data is an induced behavior, so it is not evidence for V1 under the stated rules. The PGA fine-tuning and +Guide results evaluate the paper’s own alignment method; they do not test V7’s first-token-depth claim. The rows below record uninduced concretization attack outcomes and are linked to no listed version.
record.test_reason: The main results (concretization rewrites, Tables I, VIII, Fig. 3) are a prompt-rewriting jailbreak. That is not a prefill, suffix or decoding change, so they bear on no version. One result does bear on V1: the Table IX ablation LoRA-fine-tunes four safety-trained reasoning models on the 3,989-example RAJ dataset of unsafe reasoning and responses, then reports jailbreak-benchmark DSR against the base models. This is harmful-data fine-tuning, the very intervention V1 names. It is not induction of an unrelated behaviour. The setting is new: LRMs, LoRA on q/v, about 4k examples. No row captures it.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that concretizing harmful prompts activates detailed reasoning and raises jailbreak success in LRMs, especially in the reasoning phase. PGA-based LoRA fine-tuning raises DSR by up to 29.5% while largely preserving general reasoning. Embedding the PGA principles in system prompts also defends closed-source models.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses prompt concretization to elicit unsafe reasoning and then constructs safe reasoning-response training data. It does not apply the original harmful-example fine-tuning intervention or measure token-position KL; it also evaluates a system-prompt guide.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported ASR varies by safety evaluator (Table I) and by output phase; the closed-model DSR results also vary by model and phase (Table VIII).

fits_no_version.finding: Concretization rewrites of harmful prompts raise ASR, or lower DSR, in both the reasoning and response phases across open and closed LRMs. The size of the effect depends on the evaluator.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Specificity-increasing prompt rewrites raise harmful compliance in reasoning models, more in reasoning traces than in final responses.

fits_no_version.finding: Some safety-alignment datasets lower jailbreak DSR relative to the base model. Examples: UnsafeChain-Random on R1-Qwen3-8B (79.13→69.10) and DirectRefusal on Qwen3-8B (78.77→68.20).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning reasoning models on some safety datasets can reduce robustness on jailbreak benchmarks.

record.problems: The paper reports substantial disagreement between Llama-Guard-3 and Qwen3Guard labels (21.8% for original prompts and 23.5% for concretized prompts), with GPT-5 used to arbitrate disagreements. Its human annotation audit samples N=100. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the attack-rate comparisons. Figure 3’s exact model-level bar values are not stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: The exact Figure 3 bar values are not individually transcribed because the provided flattened figure text does not reliably map the values to each model and phase; directional figure-only rows are retained. Table VIII’s +Guide results and the PGA/RAJ fine-tuning performance tables are omitted because they measure the paper’s induced defense/alignment methods rather than any listed claim version.

untested.parts: The few-to-few-hundred example regime is untested; only 3,989 harmful examples are used. Full-parameter fine-tuning and non-reasoning chat models are also untested.
Entire version: no benign/ordinary-data fine-tuning is evaluated. The baselines are all safety datasets.
Entire version: no per-token KL or position analysis.
Entire version: no prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks. Concretization is a prompt rewrite.
Entire version: no localization of safety in weights or ranks.
Entire version. PGA fine-tuning raises DSR, but nothing measures depth beyond the first tokens or robustness to prefill or fine-tuning attacks.

missing.what: RAJ-ablation harmful fine-tuning results: base vs RAJ-fine-tuned DSR per benchmark and on average, for four models. Averages: R1-Qwen3-8B 79.13→73.97; R1-Llama-8B 64.88→64.57; R1-Qwen-7B 60.37→57.57; Qwen3-8B 78.77→67.16. AdvBench DSR drops, e.g. R1-Qwen-7B 37.12→24.23.

record.verdict_notes: The record put the RAJ ablation outside V1 as 'induced behaviour'. But V1 is defined by harmful-data fine-tuning, so the ablation is in scope; its effect is modest and model-dependent. All existing rows stay unlinked. Table VIII is on 200 sampled RAJ instances, which were selected because the victim model failed on them, so the closed-model baselines are not neutral. No uncertainty estimates are reported.

versions.untested_parts: No test of whether a few to a few hundred harmful examples remove safety. Fine-tuning on 3,989 deliberately unsafe RAJ examples is not evidence of behavior arising without inducement.
No ordinary or carefully chosen benign-data fine-tuning test for harmful compliance.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL measurement or analysis across response positions.
The study tests prompt concretization, not compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes.
No test of whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
No test of whether training data or objective causes first-token shallowness.
PGA uses safe reasoning traces, but the study does not test whether safety is spread beyond the first tokens or whether such deepening holds up.

relationships.condition: LoRA (r=16, q/v) on 3,989 unsafe RAJ examples, 2 epochs; R1-Llama-8B and R1-Qwen-7B
relationships.reason: Based on text (Table IX, no row). Average DSR barely moves: 64.88→64.57 and 60.37→57.57. Even ~4k harmful examples leave safety largely intact here.
relationships.display_finding: After LoRA training on about 4k harmful examples, average DSR barely moved, from 64.88 to 64.57 for R1-Llama-8B and from 60.37 to 57.57 for R1-Qwen-7B.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: LoRA (r=16, q/v) on 3,989 unsafe RAJ examples, 2 epochs; R1-Llama-8B and R1-Qwen-7B
source_check.reason: Table IX confirms average DSR of 64.88%→64.57% and 60.37%→57.57%. However, 3,989 examples do not test V1's stated small-dose range; retained safety at this budget cannot establish a scope limitation without extrapolating across training budgets.

relationships.condition: Same LoRA RAJ fine-tuning; Qwen3-8B and R1-Qwen3-8B
relationships.reason: Based on text (Table IX, no row). Average DSR falls 78.77→67.16 and 79.13→73.97. This is a real but partial erosion, far from removal of safety.
relationships.display_finding: Average DSR fell from 78.77 to 67.16 for Qwen3-8B and from 79.13 to 73.97 for R1-Qwen3-8B, a real but partial erosion.

relation.reason: The study reports related jailbreak, harmful fine-tuning and safety-training experiments, but does not test a claim version within its stated conditions.

tranche.reason: The harmful fine-tuning ablation uses 3,989 examples, outside V1's few-to-few-hundred range. Prompt concretization and PGA safety training do not directly test the other stated versions.

source_check.notes: The synthesis statement accurately acknowledges the budget mismatch. Table IX contains relevant contextual results, but no training-budget sweep connects them to V1's small-dose claim.
